subject: Numeracy
title: Counting to three with real things
subtopics: Touch and count one at a time
objectives: Children will touch each object once while saying the number words.
Children will say or show how many when there are up to three.
content: Counting up to three real objects by touching each one once, and answering how many.
teachingActivities: Count slowly aloud with a clear touch on each object; move counted objects to one side; repeat the last number as the answer.
learnerActivities: Touch and move objects one at a time while saying the numbers; count steps, claps and jumps; answer how many.
resources: A basket of large toy vehicles
assessment: Check whether each child touches one object for each number word and says how many for groups up to three.
expectedOutcomes: Counts up to three objects with one touch for each.
Answers how many with the last number word, with support.
crossCurricular: Literacy: number words in rhymes and chants
Physical Development: moving objects one at a time
Social Habits: taking turns to count

lessons.title: Touch and say
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Touch and count one at a time
objectives: Children will touch one object for each number word when counting up to three.
successCriteria: Says the number words in order
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join the rhyme one, two, three and show one, two or three fingers.
lessons.starter: Put three blocks on the mat. Say "I have some blocks. Let me count them. I touch, I say." Touch the first block slowly and wait for the children to watch.
teacherActivities: Touch the first block and say "one". Slide it to the other tray. Touch the next and say "two", then "three".
Say "I touched three blocks. There are three." Point to all three on the tray.
Invite a child to touch and slide each block while you say the numbers slowly.
Repeat with two blocks, then one block, so the numbers change.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Children say "three" and look at the blocks.
Child touches and slides one block for each number.
Children touch and say "two" or "one" as asked.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Touch the first block and say "one". Slide it to the other tray. Touch the next and say "two", then "three". Children: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "I touched three blocks. There are three." Point to all three on the tray. Children: Children say "three" and look at the blocks.
Step 3. Teacher: Invite a child to touch and slide each block while you say the numbers slowly. Children: Child touches and slides one block for each number.
Step 4. Teacher: Repeat with two blocks, then one block, so the numbers change. Children: Children touch and say "two" or "one" as asked.

practical.title: Block count
steps: Give each pair a tray of three blocks and an empty tray.
Child one touches and slides each block while child two says the numbers.
practical.safety: Use large blocks that do not fit in a child’s mouth. Seat children firmly on the floor.

differentiation.support: Count only two blocks and guide the child’s finger with a hand-over-hand touch.
differentiation.extension: Count four blocks with help and say "four".

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks did you count?
Can you touch each block once?
questions.expected: Child touches each block one time.

expectedOutcomes: Touches one object for each number word
Says numbers one to three in order
lessons.conclusion: Slide all the blocks back into the first tray, saying "one, two, three, all home."
lessons.homeConnection: Count three spoons or three shoes at home by touching each one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch one object for each number word when counting up to three" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Touch one, touch two, touch three. Blocks and me.

lessons.title: How many cups?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will answer how many with the last number they say for up to three cups.
successCriteria: Says or shows the last number as the answer
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join the rhyme one, two, three and show one, two or three fingers.
lessons.starter: Shake the shaker and say "Listen! How many shakes?" Shake three times and count them out. Say "Now let us count something we can see."
teacherActivities: Put one cup on the tray. Say "How many cups? One." Add a second, then a third, asking each time.
Mix the cups on the tray and count them again by touching.
Say "How many?" and wait. Do not help unless needed.
Add or remove a cup and ask "How many now?"
learnerActivities: Children answer "one", "two" and "three".
Children touch each cup and say the numbers.
Children say the last number or show it with fingers.
Children count again and say the new number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put one cup on the tray. Say "How many cups? One." Add a second, then a third, asking each time. Children: Children answer "one", "two" and "three".
Step 2. Teacher: Mix the cups on the tray and count them again by touching. Children: Children touch each cup and say the numbers.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "How many?" and wait. Do not help unless needed. Children: Children say the last number or show it with fingers.
Step 4. Teacher: Add or remove a cup and ask "How many now?" Children: Children count again and say the new number.

practical.title: Cup count tray
steps: Place one to three cups on a tray for each pair.
One child counts the cups, the other shows the number on fingers.
Swap and play again with a different number.
practical.safety: Use unbreakable cups only. Keep cups on the tray and off the floor to avoid slips.

differentiation.support: Offer one or two cups only and say the number with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count three cups and then give you exactly two.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups are on the tray?
questions.expected: The correct number, up to three.

questions.question: Show me with your fingers.
questions.expected: Child shows the number of fingers.

expectedOutcomes: Answers how many up to three
lessons.conclusion: Stack the cups one by one while counting, then tip them back on the tray and say "Three cups. Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask "how many?" when your child has biscuits, shoes or toys, up to three.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "answer how many with the last number they say for up to three cups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting steps, claps and jumps
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count steps, claps or jumps up to three.
successCriteria: Takes one step for each number
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join the rhyme one, two, three and show one, two or three fingers.
resources: Three footprints cut from paper or card
lessons.starter: Walk three big steps across the floor and say "One, two, three! I walked three steps." Ask "Can you walk three steps?"
teacherActivities: Place three paper footprints on the floor in a line. Step on each one and say the numbers.
Call out "Walk two steps" and do it. Then "Walk three steps".
Change to clapping: "Clap three." then to jumping: "Jump two."
Let a child choose a number and call it for the group.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Children walk the number of steps called and stop.
Children clap or jump the number called.
Child calls a number from one to three and the group does it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place three paper footprints on the floor in a line. Step on each one and say the numbers. Children: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Call out "Walk two steps" and do it. Then "Walk three steps". Children: Children walk the number of steps called and stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Change to clapping: "Clap three." then to jumping: "Jump two." Children: Children clap or jump the number called.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child choose a number and call it for the group. Children: Child calls a number from one to three and the group does it.

practical.title: Footprint walk
steps: Lay three footprints in a line.
Each child steps on them while the group counts.
Repeat with two and then one footprint.
practical.safety: Fix paper footprints with tape so they do not slip. Children walk one at a time with an adult nearby.

differentiation.support: Walk beside the child and touch the shoulder at each step.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to do three claps and two jumps in a row.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many steps did you take?
questions.expected: The number of steps, up to three.

expectedOutcomes: Moves the number of times called
lessons.conclusion: Take three slow steps to the sitting area and count them. Sit down together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count steps to the door or the gate at home, one to three.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count steps, claps or jumps up to three" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting toy vehicles
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count toy vehicles in play and answer how many.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join the rhyme one, two, three and show one, two or three fingers.
resources: A mat road or drawn road
lessons.starter: Push a toy car along the road and say "Brum, brum, how many cars on the road? Let us count them."
teacherActivities: Place one, two or three vehicles on the road. Ask "How many vehicles?" and touch each one as you count.
Say "Park two vehicles." Move two vehicles to the car park.
Say "How many are still on the road?" Let children look and answer.
Pass the basket and ask each child to take three vehicles and count them.
learnerActivities: Children count with you and say the last number.
Child moves two vehicles and counts them.
Children count the vehicles on the road.
Child takes vehicles and counts up to three.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place one, two or three vehicles on the road. Ask "How many vehicles?" and touch each one as you count. Children: Children count with you and say the last number.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Park two vehicles." Move two vehicles to the car park. Children: Child moves two vehicles and counts them.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "How many are still on the road?" Let children look and answer. Children: Children count the vehicles on the road.
Step 4. Teacher: Pass the basket and ask each child to take three vehicles and count them. Children: Child takes vehicles and counts up to three.

practical.title: Road count
steps: Put a road mat on the floor.
Children place up to three vehicles on the road and count them.
They tell a friend how many.
practical.safety: Toy vehicles must be too large to swallow and have no loose parts; keep them off the floor between turns.

differentiation.support: Use only two vehicles and say each number as the child touches them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put three vehicles on the road, take one away and say how many are left.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many vehicles on the road?
questions.expected: The correct number, up to three.

questions.question: Can you park one vehicle?
questions.expected: Child moves one vehicle and counts it.

lessons.conclusion: Park all the vehicles in the basket while counting them aloud.
lessons.homeConnection: Count cars or okadas you see on the road and say how many.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count toy vehicles in play and answer how many" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can count up to three at three stations.
successCriteria: Says how many up to three
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join the rhyme one, two, three and show one, two or three fingers.
lessons.starter: Show each station and say "Count, count, count with me." Remind the children to touch each one.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch whether each child touches one object for each number.
Note each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children count at each station.
Child counts and answers.
Children continue and tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children count at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch whether each child touches one object for each number. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Note each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children continue and tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items and supervise each station closely.

differentiation.support: Offer an adult partner at each station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count objects for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: touches one object for each number; says how many up to three; counts steps, claps or jumps.

questions.question: How many blocks?
questions.expected: The correct number, up to three.

questions.question: Can you count the cups again?
questions.expected: Child counts again and gets the same number.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Count the children sitting on the mat together, up to three at a time.
lessons.homeConnection: Count to three each day with a real object such as fruit or shoes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can count up to three at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
